steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in potatoes, Italian seasoning, paprika, and garlic salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are reddish brown and tender, about 12 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Spiced Up Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: This quick and easy recipe for canned potatoes turns simple sliced spuds into a spectacularly seasoned side dish that can be served with any main course.
raw_recipe.name: Spiced Up Potatoes

recipeInstructions.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in potatoes, Italian seasoning, paprika, and garlic salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are reddish brown and tender, about 12 minutes.

review.reviewBody:
I’m so glad I went for it. I almost didn’t. 
What I love about this site is you can type in a specific ingredient and recipes will come up for that ingredient. Today, I had canned potatoes and it brought me to this recipe. I always read reviews…always. It helps to see what others who’ve tried the recipe think of it. What I don’t understand are reviews when the original ‘main’ ingredient is completely changed due to ‘preference’. This was a recipe for ‘canned’ potatoes. The reviews almost made me not try this because they were (almost) all about using ‘real’ potatoes. 
I mixed all the ingredients in a bowl and then put it into the pan (the before picture). I did use garlic powder instead of salt as some suggested. I added parsley towards the end of the cooking time. At 12 minutes they were fine - I like mine browner so I let it go another 2 minutes. Finished product was great! (the after picture) Thank you Jodi Smith for a wonderful way to perk up some canned potatoes. This recipe will be a go-to for me when I have canned potatoes on hand. SIDE NOTE: It's really important to drain the potatoes and rinse thoroughly.

Desperate to use two cans of sliced potatoes, I tried this yesterday morning and was pleasantly surprised. I added sauteed onions and ground pepper and the dish was a hit! Great in a pinch when fresh are not readily available. One thing - these potatoes are very wet when they are just out of the can. Drain and also pat down with paper towels to remove some of the excess moisture.

This was really easy. I mostly followed the recipe. The only difference was that I seasoned them to my liking, added frozen fajita veggies, and fried them until they were really golden brown and crispy. Other than that, quick and easy . Also.....if a recipe's MAIN ingredient is changed, then it's not really not the recipe anymore, is it? Why would you look up a canned potatoes recipe to use on fresh potatoes? Make it make sense please! Don't rip on the recipe if you think the main ingredient is gross, it just brings down the rating for people that are really wanting to use the main ingredient.

Goodness this recipe needs revised. 4 tsp of paprika?? NO WAY!! It only needs 1 tsp, my goodness. And only 2 tsps of Italian seasoning. I used garlic oil instead of butter, so much better, and only 1/4 tsp of salt. Then I topped if with a little bit of Parmesan cheese.

I’ve made this several times now, it’s easy and they are amazing. Sometimes I sauté some onions in with them, and I will add a little bit of Two Gringos Chupacabra Brisket seasoning as well. Outstanding and easy recipe.

This wasn't bad. I used fresh potatoes since I don't use canned potatoes. I used fresh garlic instead of the salt. I decreased the paprika by a third but it was still way too much, next time I will decrease it by two-thirds. Since I used fresh potatoes, I simmered them in water for a few minutes and then plunged them in cold water before beginning the saute because I feared they would be a little hard. Turned out great other than the excess paprika, which is why I gave it 3 stars.
I changed the garlic salt to powder as recommended in comments, and added two teaspoons of dry dill seasoning.

I have canned potatoes and let them sit in the cabinet because I couldn't stand them. Then I figured, someone has had to do something with those! And the rest, as they say, is history. They were delicious! I had everything but the paprika, will have to get. And I use garlic powder, not salt, so I added some sea salt. Next time, I will turn the heat up and cook them a little crispier. But all in all, I found something tasty and easy to do with those potatoes. What I did not get was people remarking about canned vs fresh potatoes. The recipe was for "canned potatoes". And I, for one, am grateful.
Great use for a difficult product. I added a bit of cayenne and at the end topped with shredded American cheese. Yeah, that works. Next time ill add onions.
Way to much of Italian seasoning. Could not taste paprika. The potatoes were not red. Will go halves on the Italian seasoning next time

Boy did I have to revamp this recipe! I had two cans of sliced potatoes that I needed to use as they were purchased by mistake (long story) anyway I changed up the seasoning and then baked them in the oven. The consistency of canned potatoes is too soft to sauté.
I fried the potatoes in Bacon Up, onion, garlic powder, paprika and Kinders Buttery Steakhouse seasoning. Came out delicious

I really didn't like the Italian Seasoning in this recipe (the taste AND the texture). Even if I cut the amount in half, I still wouldn't care for the texture. I would eliminate it next time and try adding a little onion powder. I usually don't use canned potatoes because they taste tinny to me, but I had a couple of cans in my prepper pantry that I needed to use. I did think the spices covered up the tinny taste.
The flavor was okay but unless you have a very very very very large skillet you should cut the recipe in half because the potatoes won't Brown. So yeah cut this recipe in half and it should be fine

This is an okay recipe. However, I just could not bring myself to use that much Italian seasoning, paprika, and garlic salt; so, I halved the amounts of each and it turned out just fine. Also, I halved the butter and added a bit of bacon fat instead.
I added a little extra spices that the recipe already called for. It was super yummy 😋
I used something called magic dust. you can make it off the internet. excelent
Still cooking atm, but they smell so delicious
I made it just as it says, and I’ll never avoid canned potatoes again. It was a huge hit with the 6 others in my family! Even my super picky youngest loved them
